title: Preterite or imperfect?
summary: Completed event or background? Cuando llegué, llovía. Mientras cenábamos, sonó el teléfono.
focus: Choosing between the preterite and the imperfect
content:
## Photo or video?

Both tenses talk about the past. They differ in how you look at it.

- The **preterite** is a **photo**: a completed action, seen as one whole, often counted or dated. *Ayer comí paella. Vivió tres años en Madrid. Llamé dos veces.*
- The **imperfect** is a **video**: something going on, repeated or simply true at the time, with no start or end in view. *Comía paella todos los domingos. Vivía en Madrid. Llovía.*

The same verb can take either; it depends on what you mean:

- *Trabajé en un bar.*: I worked in a bar (done, over).
- *Trabajaba en un bar.*: I was working / used to work in a bar (the situation then).

## Cuando + preterite, mientras + imperfect

Two connectors usually go with a particular tense:

- **cuando** introduces the **event** that happens: *Cuando llegué a casa, llovía.* (When I got home, it was raining.)
- **mientras** introduces the **ongoing** background: *Mientras cenábamos, sonó el teléfono.* (While we were having dinner, the phone rang.)

**De repente** (suddenly) always announces a preterite: *De repente oímos un ruido.* (Suddenly we heard a noise.)

When two actions simply follow each other, both are preterite: *Entré, cerré la puerta y me senté.*

## Estaba… cuando…

The classic story pattern is a scene in the imperfect, then an event in the preterite that interrupts it.

- *Estaba durmiendo cuando sonó el teléfono.*: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
- *Eran las ocho y los niños jugaban en la calle cuando empezó a llover.*: It was eight and the children were playing in the street when it started to rain.
- *Hacía mucho frío, no había nadie y, de repente, vi a Marta.*: It was very cold, there was nobody around and, suddenly, I saw Marta.

The setting (time, weather, feelings, what people were doing) takes the imperfect. What happened next takes the preterite.

## Verbs that change meaning

A few verbs shift in English translation depending on the tense, because the preterite turns a state into an event:

| verb | imperfect (state) | preterite (event) |
|---|---|---|
| conocer | *conocía* = I knew (someone) | *conocí* = I met |
| saber | *sabía* = I knew (a fact) | *supe* = I found out |
| querer | *quería* = I wanted | *quise* = I tried; *no quise* = I refused |
| poder | *podía* = I was able (in general) | *pude* = I managed; *no pude* = I failed to |
| tener que | *tenía que* = I was supposed to | *tuve que* = I had to (and did) |

- *Conocí a mi mujer en Granada.*: I met my wife in Granada.
- *Ayer supe la noticia.*: Yesterday I found out the news.
- *Tuve que trabajar hasta las diez.*: I had to work until ten.

quiz.prompt: Ayer, cuando ___ (yo, llegar) a casa, llovía mucho.
quiz.explanation: 'Cuando' introduces the event (arriving), a completed action on a specific day: preterite 'llegué'. The rain is the background, so 'llovía'.
hints: The rain is the video; arriving is the photo.

quiz.explanation: 'Mientras' introduces the ongoing background, so the imperfect: 'cenábamos'. The phone ringing interrupts it in the preterite.

quiz.prompt: Estaba durmiendo cuando de repente ___ un ruido.
quiz.explanation: 'De repente' announces a sudden, completed event: preterite 'oí'. 'Estaba durmiendo' is the scene it interrupts.

quiz.prompt: ___ (yo, conocer) a mi mujer en Granada en 2010.
quiz.explanation: Meeting someone for the first time is an event, so the preterite: 'conocí' = I met. 'Conocía' would mean I already knew her.
Not knowing how to swim is a state that lasted through childhood: imperfect 'sabía'. 'Supe' would mean I found out.
hints: A state in the past → imperfect.

quiz.prompt: Ayer ___ (yo, saber) la noticia por mi hermana.
quiz.explanation: Finding out is the moment knowledge begins, an event: preterite 'supe' = I found out.
hints: Preterite of saber = to find out.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'He refused to talk to me'?
quiz.explanation: 'No quiso' in the preterite is a decision taken: he refused. 'No quería' only says he didn't feel like it; 'no quiere' is present.
hints: Refusing is an event, not a mood.

quiz.prompt: Anoche ___ (yo, tener) que trabajar hasta las diez.
quiz.explanation: 'Tuve que' = I had to and I did it, a completed obligation on a specific night. 'Tenía que' would mean I was supposed to (and maybe didn't).

quiz.prompt: Which sentence is correct for 'It was eight o'clock and the children were playing when the phone rang'?
options: Eran las ocho y los niños jugaban cuando sonó el teléfono.
Fueron las ocho y los niños jugaron cuando sonaba el teléfono.
Eran las ocho y los niños jugaban cuando sonaba el teléfono.
quiz.correct_answer: Eran las ocho y los niños jugaban cuando sonó el teléfono.
quiz.explanation: Time and what was going on are the scene (imperfect: eran, jugaban); the phone ringing is the event that interrupts it (preterite: sonó).

guide.tip: Ask two questions: Is this what happened (preterite), or what was going on while it happened (imperfect)?

conversations.title: What happened last night?
conversations.scenario: Laura looks tired. Javi asks her what happened last night and she tells the story.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Laura, tienes mala cara. ¿Qué te pasó anoche?
lines.meaning: Laura, you look rough. What happened to you last night?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Uf. Eran las once y yo estaba durmiendo tranquilamente cuando, de repente, sonó el teléfono.
lines.meaning: Ugh. It was eleven and I was sleeping peacefully when, suddenly, the phone rang.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Era mi hermana. Me dijo que su coche no arrancaba y que estaba sola en la carretera.
lines.meaning: It was my sister. She told me her car wouldn't start and that she was alone on the road.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Oh no! And what did you do?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tuve que vestirme y salir a buscarla. Llovía mucho y no había casi nadie en la calle.
lines.meaning: I had to get dressed and go out to find her. It was raining hard and there was almost nobody in the street.
lines.note: tuve que: did it · llovía, había: background

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Did you know where she was exactly?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, no lo sabía. Lo supe cuando me mandó la ubicación. Llegué a la una y media.
lines.meaning: No, I didn't. I found out when she sent me her location. I got there at half past one.
lines.note: sabía (knew) vs supe (found out) · llegué: event

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: And did you manage to fix the car?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, no pude. Mientras esperábamos a la grúa, conocimos a un vecino muy amable que nos trajo café.
lines.meaning: No, I couldn't. While we were waiting for the tow truck, we met a very kind neighbour who brought us coffee.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bueno, al menos la historia tiene un final feliz. ¡Vete a dormir!
lines.meaning: Well, at least the story has a happy ending. Go and get some sleep!

bites.title: Photo vs. video
bites.rule: Preterite = a photo: one completed action (ayer comí). Imperfect = a video: what was going on or used to happen (comía todos los días).
bites.example: Trabajé en un bar. Trabajaba en un bar.
bites.example_meaning: I worked in a bar (done). I used to work in a bar (back then).

bites.title: cuando / mientras
bites.rule: Cuando introduces the event (preterite); mientras introduces the background (imperfect). De repente always brings a preterite.
bites.example_meaning: While we were having dinner, the phone rang.

bites.title: Estaba… cuando…
bites.rule: Set the scene in the imperfect (time, weather, what people were doing), then interrupt it with a preterite.
bites.example: Estaba durmiendo cuando oí un ruido.
bites.example_meaning: I was sleeping when I heard a noise.

bites.title: Meaning changers
bites.rule: conocía = knew / conocí = met; sabía = knew / supe = found out; quería = wanted / no quise = refused; tenía que = was supposed to / tuve que = had to and did.
bites.example: Conocí a mi mujer en Granada.
bites.example_meaning: I met my wife in Granada.

sorts.title: Preterite or imperfect?
sorts.why: Dated or sudden completed actions are preterite. Habits, time, weather and ongoing actions are imperfect.

sorts.title: Which Spanish verb?
sorts.why: The preterite turns a state (knowing) into an event (meeting, finding out).

sorts.title: Cuando or mientras?
sorts.why: Cuando points at the moment something happened; mientras at what was going on around it.

spots.sentence: Estábamos cenando y de repente sonaba el teléfono.
spots.why: 'De repente' marks a sudden event: preterite sonó.

spots.sentence: Conocía a mi mujer en Granada en 2010.
spots.why: Meeting someone on a date is an event: conocí = I met.

spots.sentence: Cuando era pequeño, siempre comí en casa de mi abuela.
spots.why: 'Siempre' with a childhood habit takes the imperfect: comía.

spots.sentence: Estaba durmiendo cuando oía un ruido.
spots.why: The noise interrupts the scene, so it is a preterite event: oí.
Not knowing how to swim was a state through childhood: sabía. Supe = found out.

spots.sentence: Eran las ocho cuando llegaba mi hermana.
spots.why: The time is the scene (eran); the arrival is the event: llegó.
